This research employs the Transformer model, expanding its language model capabilities to process code-mixed texts, a prevalent feature of online data, by integrating positional encoding techniques initially used in attention mechanisms. Additionally, the study incorporates a technique called Language Mixing Prohibition (LMP) that reduces model interactions between individual languages to achieve better performance. A novel, code-mixed dataset called vi6-20M, containing over 20 million samples, was developed to test the model performance across five distinct code-mixing language combinations, namely Hindi and English with Urdu, and Hindi with Sanskrit, while employing English as the target language. Experimental outcomes on the newly created dataset demonstrate that the proposed model, coupled with the LMP and positional encoding techniques, yields substantial improvements in tasks such as sentiment analysis and document classification when contrasted with Baseline models and other cutting-edge models.

Recent studies using quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations have explored the phenomenon of isotope dilution in H$_{3}$S, examining the coefficient of the isotope effect ($\eta$) at various pressures and temperatures. At low pressures, the coefficient is predominantly influenced by vibrational modes associated with hydrogen atoms, whereas increased pressure leads to predominant contributions from phonons in the S-H bonds. Isotope dilution was observed at high temperatures and low pressures but can be reduced through higher pressures or temperatures that minimize hydrogen-vibron contributions. These findings imply that high-pressure hydrogen can be efficiently stored in compound materials, such as hydrides, without inducing isotope dilution in certain situations.

Motion planning in complex spaces can be intensely computationally challenging due to the vast number of spatial constraints in the environment. Traditionally, motion planners have attempted to generate these constraints on the fly as needed, but this approach can be inefficient, especially when the environment's spatial constraints don't directly impact motion plans. We present an innovative method for generating spatial constraints offline by simulating an environment's obstacles as deformable objects, which can be integrated into any motion planning framework. We evaluated our approach in comparison to state-of-the-art motion planners and motion planning with real-time collision avoidance, demonstrating significant performance improvements in similar scenarios.

Camera relinking across distinct datasets often faces significant challenges due to differences in lighting conditions, particularly in literature research. To address this problem, our solution focuses on using deep learning techniques to enhance feature descriptors' robustness to lighting variations. By leveraging the power of adversarial training methods, we can improve the performance of descriptors and use them to obtain more reliable correspondences for camera repositioning. To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, we created a new dataset called LOCLIC, which features 20 scenes containing varied lighting conditions. According to our experimental results, the proposed method outperforms existing techniques, leading to a 72% improvement in camera repositioning accuracy and 85% in pose estimation precision.

In 5G systems, large scale MIMO technology is used to increase capacity, but it is vulnerable to interference. To address this issue, we apply group LASSO to maximize sum-rate and interfere with management in MIMO systems with multiple users. By utilizing group LASSO, we achieve two main advantages - the number of data symbols that need to be transmitted is significantly reduced and the performance in challenging channel conditions is improved, such as when there is equal power and strong interference. Our approach is even more effective when combined with other methods to manage interference and outperforms traditional baselines when tested using real data from a cellular network. Our LASSO-based approach is applied to different scenarios and we show that it can be used effectively in a variety of situations by rewriting the optimization problem in a different way. Our approach is also more efficient because it can solve problems and transmit signals more efficiently by utilizing a different value for the LASSO parameter. Our results show that our approach achieves good performance and is more efficient than other methods because it can solve problems more quickly.

This investigation focuses on the impact of a type of mapping on rational function semifields when one curve is the result of a finite harmonic transformation from another curve. Through a pull-back operation, we examine the effect of this type of mapping on semifields associated with the transformed and original curves, revealing that only a limited category of such transformations yield unique, non-trivial results. Specifically, we find these transformations are equivalent to mappings that create duplicate copies of points or mappings that establish a correlation between points and their order on the original curve. Consequently, semilattices of such transformations do not possess enough structure to be considered as a basis for a new class of tropical functions. In contrast, similar analyses indicate that similar results do not apply to the pull-back of rational value semifields under a general finite harmonic transformation.

This study provides conditions for a Markov process to possess a unique, converging quasi-stationary distribution when conditioned on its state space, given that it also satisfies the weak Doeblin condition. Additionally, some quasi-stationary distributions are shown to meet a certain regularity criterion, leading to a demonstration of path convergence. Furthermore, a non-stationary subsequence can be identified within a stationary sequence of quasi-stationary distributions, and this subsequence converges uniformly to a specific function that is in $L^{\infty}$. To validate these results, a quasi-stationary random walk on a tree is presented as an example. This research also addresses a related open question concerning the relationship between quasi-stationary distributions and invariant functions.

Building on the findings of part I, researchers investigate the connection between the transfer of $K(\pi, 1)$-structures and the integration of certain cocycles, which has implications for understanding the relationship between Bott's knot invariants and Chern--Simons theory in part II. In a technical appendix, the proof of a crucial localization principle, essential for validating the integration process, is provided.

We've used a technique called elastoresistance to study the ability of nematic fluctuations to order and deform LiFeAs and NaFeAs in their undoped states. The elastoresistance measurements reveal a significant and reversible change in resistance in LiFeAs when under strain, but strain has no effect on NaFeAs. A linear relationship between this resistance change and applied strain exists for both materials up to a certain point. Furthermore, we observe a strain-induced change in LiFeAs that is similar to what has been previously observed in ferromagnetic NaFeAs, but we find no evidence of a magnetic phase transition in LiFeAs. Based on these findings, we believe that nematic fluctuations exist in LiFeAs and are similar in strength to those found in NaFeAs, and that these fluctuations cause elastoresistance by modifying the orientation of charge carriers within the material, resulting in a similar phenomenon in both LiFeAs and NaFeAs.

In this research, we investigate a wide range of Type-II two Higgs doublet models that meet two criteria: the theoretical limits of stability and the electroweak symmetry, as well as the experimental findings of the LHC's 13 TeV data regarding the charge and diphoton decay processes of the Higgs boson. The study demonstrates that, in order to comply with the theoretical limits of perturbativity and the electroweak symmetry, the parameter space of the Higgs boson's interactions is substantial and reflects a characteristic expansion of its diphoton decay width. The observed results also show that the LHC's data have significantly narrowed the possible values of the Higgs boson's charge coupling relative to the standard model. A large dataset from the standard model's four-lepton processes further indicates that the Higgs boson's interactions remain standard-like. Utilizing these findings, we have derived new bounds on the Higgs boson's charge coupling and established a 95% confidence limit of |$\lambda_{\phi\gamma\gamma}$| $<$ 0.25 TeV$^{-4}$ on its diphoton decay width. The study highlights the importance of incorporating various search channels to accurately measure the Higgs boson's interactions.

Building complex materials from individual components requires innovative problem-solving, but AI algorithms can tackle this challenge. The problem is framed as a sequential decision-making process: at each step, the algorithm selects a new piece to add to the material based on an attempt to optimize a desired properties. The learning algorithm processes the material's assembly history, distinguishing between intentionally-designed and randomly-assembled materials to create effective policies. The property in question can vary, such as mechanical, thermal, optical, or magnetic properties. The researchers applied a Q-learning approach, incorporating a recurrent neural network to process the material's assembly history, enabling the discovery of designed and exploratory materials, as well as the development of optimal policies for a range of properties. The study differentiates between directed and exploratory design, aiming to discover both naturally occurring and artificially induced patterns in exploratory assemblies. The researchers assigned scores to both directed and exploratory designs, weighted by their frequency, to create diverse and potentially better materials. The study discovered that designed and exploratory materials exhibited distinct patterns in assembly order, highlighting the potential for exploring random designs as a source of materials with superior properties.

We utilize the variational method in the temporal boundary conditions to analyze the Dyson-Schwinger equations in the Landau gauge. Our results show that in any confining flavor-symmetric vacuum of a chiral gauge theory, the 't Hooft anomaly matching equations are satisfied. This conclusion is crucial as it provides a basis for analyzing properties of hadrons in the large N limit without relying on perturbation theory. Furthermore, we apply the anomaly-matching principle in a model where the SU(3) flavor symmetry is non-linearly realized, providing a new theoretical framework for analyzing large N limit behavior. This framework is distinct from well-established results on chiral Lagrangian constraints and the large N limit properties of mesons.

We have provided the most direct proof possible to demonstrate the well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations in certain critical Besov spaces and P-Besov spaces. We have achieved this by specifically addressing potential issues related to the continuity of generalized solutions and thus precluding the use of recent results from intermittent analysis of parabolic equations. We have established that the Navier-Stokes equations are well-posed for the spaces $\dot{B}_{d, 2}^{-2}$ and P$\dot{B}_{d, 2}^{0}$ when the initial data is small enough relative to their respective critical norms. We have also shown that the same space-critical conditions apply to the solutions obtained through the Galerkin method. We have further extended these findings to cover a range of critical and supra-critical cases, including the Trudinger-Moser type critical case. We have also extended our results to cover the case of data that is non-periodic and belong to the $L^{3}\cap V^{2}$ space.

A comprehensive model of the electronic and magnetic properties of antiferromagnetic systems with a spin-1/2 lattice has been studied using computational physics. The study incorporates thermal fluctuations in the parameters through a finite-temperature Landau-Lifshitz method and utilizes a tight-binding model to determine the electronic structure. The analysis shows that temperature-dependent magnon bandgap and resonance modes emerge due to thermal magnon interactions. Interestingly, at high temperatures, the model reveals the presence of a Fermi-liquid state with highly anisotropic hole and electron quasiparticle weights. The study also indicates that Dirac cones are a stable feature across all temperature ranges. However, the model predicts the presence of Van Hove singularities on the density-of-states, despite the absence of such singularities in the band structure. The study's findings exhibit quantitative consistency with experimental data on the normal state quasiparticle weights of high-temperature superconductors.

This paper introduces a novel idea to utilize a quantum one-way quantum transformation (1OWQT) for developing a one-time pad (OTTP) cryptosystem. The OTTP method enhances the security of data transmission by using a publicly generated key to encrypt and decrypt information via a secure, public channel. Building upon this concept, our study presents two enhanced quantum cryptosystem designs based on 1OWQTs, which utilize a more robust and efficient quantum channel to increase security and efficiency. The first design improves public-key size and information transmission rates by combining two distinct 1OWQTs, while the second employs a more stable and high-capacity 2-qubit 1OWQT based on the quantum teleportation protocol. To make OTTP more practical, our method generates keys in a parallel fashion, eliminating the previous requirement for sequential key production. Additionally, our method enhances key security by integrating direct and indirect quantum error correction.

Advanced language models have achieved impressive results across various NLP tasks by leveraging large pre-trained models. Despite this success, these models continue to struggle with accurately understanding and generating rare words. To address this limitation, we propose the BERT-based Rare Word Model (BERM), which effectively utilizes the surrounding context to improve the representation and understanding of rare words. Firstly, we pre-trained a rare word embedding table using rare word replacement, using BERT as the feature extractor. Subsequently, we integrated the word embedding table into a BERT-based model for targeted rare word prediction tasks. Through thorough evaluation on six datasets, we demonstrated that BERM achieves significantly better results compared to existing methods, achieving up to a 4.13 F1-2 score improvement. Notably, our approach is also applicable to BERT models pre-trained on smaller datasets, resulting in a 2.53 F1-2 score improvement. Furthermore, we explored the application of BERM to BERT-based multi-task learning, achieving impressive results on targeted datasets with a 2.04 F1-2 score improvement. Overall, our work provides a practical solution for addressing the rare word problem within BERT-based models, while also facilitating further research on this issue.

Researchers obtained a new set of results for the properties of the extremal weights of a random Minimum Spanning Acycle in an ordered weighted graph. The findings showed that the statistical distributions of these weights converge to a specific probability distribution that generalizes the behaviors of the extremal weights of a random spanning tree. The results also provided a non-negative weight assignment that closely approximates the extremal weights of a random Minimum Spanning Acycle, similar to the properties seen in a random spanning tree. The findings were theoretically verified to show that the rate at which the extremal weights converge to zero follows a specific power law for a specific class of graphs. The research also provided methods to estimate the parameters of the resulting probability distribution. The researchers conducted a series of experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of their methods and found that they performed well on a variety of graphs. The findings have significant implications as they generalize the properties seen in a random spanning tree to a different class of graphs. The research also provides a different algorithm to produce a non-negative weight assignment that closely approximates the extremal weights of a random Minimum Spanning Acycle. The methods proposed in the research can be used in a number of applications, including the analysis of complex systems. The researchers' methods have a significant advantage over previous methods used to analyze random spanning cycles as they produce more accurate results with fewer weight assignments. The remaining sections of the thesis provide additional details on the different topics covered in the research, including a review of the existing literature and

This study presents a novel vertical FL attack capable of accurately reconstructing private images even with minimal data, as it demonstrates with mProstateX, a large prostate cancer imaging database. FL protocols share image data in encrypted form with a server, but our approach bypasses this encryption by uncovering the shared images. We achieved this by training a unique model to identify FL image patches, which are then combined to reconstruct the shared image. This approach successfully reconstructed mProstateX images from FL data with remarkable accuracy, and also applied to FL medical images with chest X-rays. Moreover, our results show that by processing only 1% of FL data, we can reconstruct nearly 51% of the original images, and even with as little as 0.1% of the data, we can reconstruct around 21% of the original images. This finding highlights a severe vulnerability in vertical FL protocols, particularly in sensitive fields like healthcare where FL is increasingly utilized.

Utilizing the light-cone non-relativistic quark-diquark description, researchers have computed the rate of $B^+ \to p \bar{\Lambda}$ along with the associated $B^+ \to p \bar{\Lambda} \gamma$ process in theoretical frameworks. The findings suggest that if a dark antibaryon exists with an mass around the nucleon mass, the $B^+ \to p \bar{\Lambda} \gamma$ process could be observed with a rate comparable to that of $B^+ \to p \bar{\Psi}$, where $\bar{\Psi}$ represents a dark baryon. The decay width of $B^+ \to p \bar{\Psi}$ is found to be sensitive to the dark particle's mass and the associated dark coupling. Assuming that the dark particle has a strangeness-like property, researchers have calculated the rate of $B^+ \to p \bar{\Lambda} \gamma$ using QCD light-cone sum rules and found it to be around $10^{-8}$ GeV. The findings suggest that if the mass of the dark particle is higher than its associated partner mass, the rate of $B^+ \to p \bar{\Psi}$ could be observed with a higher probability. The findings of this research provide insights into how to effectively search for dark particles using semileptonic decays of B-mesons.

Current approaches for distributing resources among separate entities within the context of counterterrorism are generally centralized, controlled by a single authority, and based on a unified framework. However, when dealing with complex scenarios involving multiple entities with varying levels of capability and constraint, a centralized approach can be impractical. In this study, we introduce a novel distributed learning strategy to facilitate cooperation and resource sharing between competing entities, each operating under distinct limitations. Employing a game-theoretic framework, we demonstrate a robust convergence method for entities operating independently, allocating their own resources under a decentralized budgeting system. Our results show that, through independent decision-making, entities become aware of a shared, consistent resource allocation strategy. Furthermore, when entities adhere to a unified budgeting system, a distributed learning method enables them to converge towards a optimal strategy for cooperative defense against terrorist threats. Comprehensive numerical assessments validate the efficacy of our proposed approaches.

A model of a spherical cavity containing a scalar field and a charged black hole, both thermodynamic and phase transition behaviors are investigated in this study.  The results show a universal electric potential-dependent threshold in the phase transition behavior of the scalar field and the black hole.  Further, we demonstrate how the model can be extended to higher-dimensional spaces and discuss the implications of our findings.

This research introduces an innovative sampling strategy for bag of words, dubbed bag sampling, to enhance long document ranking on a large scale. The proposed technique completes documents ranking on a massive level using features and full documents. To facilitate real-time processing, a novel sampling strategy is proposed to minimize required features for documents. The proposed technique achieves an average of 99% accuracy for non-selected documents and outperforms the state-of-the-art model by 0.01 in MapReduce, achieving a convergence rate 5 times faster. The proposed technique also significantly reduces memory consumption by document type.

Graph Neural Networks have achieved significant success in semi-supervised node classification tasks. A key challenge arises when dealing with limited labeled data, necessitating a high-quality pseudo-labeling strategy to overcome this constraint. Current pseudo-labeling methods primarily rely on the supervised classifier's initial predictions on unlabeled nodes, often leading to inaccurate labels and consequently suboptimal model performance. To address this issue, we introduce a novel pseudo-labeling approach for GNNs, known as Guided Pseudo-Labeling for GNNs (GP-GNN), which constructs refined pseudo-labels through a two-stage process. First, it leverages both local and global representations to separate classes, then fuses these with initial model predictions to produce refined pseudo-labels. Furthermore, our approach incorporates a guided regularization term to prevent information in underfit models from being misinterpreted. GP-GNN not only improves pseudo-label quality but also allows the model to benefit from a regularized training process. We evaluate GP-GNN extensively using real-world datasets and experimentally demonstrate that it yields superior results compared to existing pseudo-labeling strategies, ultimately illustrating its effectiveness in semi-supervised node classification tasks.

The use of betatron radiation from an electron beam oscillation to accelerate particles is a well-established concept in plasma wakefield acceleration techniques, particularly in the context of X-ray radiation sources and colliders. However, a major challenge posed by this method is the mismatch in the sizes of the accelerated beams, resulting in reduced cross-section for interaction and beam dynamics. In this research, we have revisited this issue in the context of EWLA, an X-ray radiation source based on plasma wakefield acceleration, and have identified a specific threshold for radial mismatch that can jeopardize its performance. To overcome this limitation, we have explored the potential of rotating the electron beam, acting as a "spatial lens", and other beam manipulation tactics to mitigate the effects of size mismatch. Our findings suggest that these methods are feasible and may be a critical factor in determining EWLA's effectiveness. In light of this, we propose an approach to optimize beam interaction by adjusting the phase and amplitude of the electron beam oscillation. Furthermore, we have developed a simplified model for corotation synchronization and have identified key criteria for ensuring that the electron beam remains confined. Notably, our research has revealed that a small initial perturbation in the electron beam distribution can help to compensate for radial mismatch, offering a promising strategy for beam reconfiguration and performance optimization.

This paper presents an application of differentially private decision tree learning with the constraints of a labeled public dataset and an unlabeled public reference. A novel, two-stage learning framework is developed to build a differentially private classifier, which consists of a initial estimation of classification accuracy, a propagation of confidence across accuracy estimates, and a method to account for deviations from expected accuracy estimates. Experimental results using the public datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by achieving predicted classification accuracy rather than random noise, and revealing that its accuracy increases with growing dataset size. Furthermore, using a Gaussian mechanism to add differential privacy results in a method that tolerates slightly larger noise variances without loss of accuracy compared to using Laplace mechanism. Additionally, this approach maintains accuracy by introducing less noise into the learning process by shifting classification errors from leaf node predictions to accuracy estimates, and allowing for a trade-off of accuracy for privacy by adjusting the noise variance.

This research proposes a novel algorithm based on a relaxed moment-matching method to optimize the regularized R'enyi divergence, addressing a lingering challenge in the field. By expanding upon existing work that proved the duality between optimizing the divergence and a sequence of probabilistic quadratic programming problems, our algorithm deviates from the standard maximum a posteriori (MAP) solution by introducing additional degrees of freedom to the Lagrangian dual function. In essence, this modification permits the incorporation of moment-matching constraints at every stage, enabling the solution to diverge from the MAP strategy while still maintaining consistency with the original optimization problem. Similar to the reparameterization-based methods, our algorithm can take advantage of this strategy to sample from the manifold of the optimal solution, which is expressed in terms of orthogonal score matching variables. Unlike existing methods, our approach does not necessitate an initial approximation of the regularization term, which is not easily amenable to sampling. Consequently, our algorithm averages over numerous random samples during the optimization process, which is found to generalizes effectively and performs well across a range of different regularizers.

In the field of Bayesian spatial analysis, traditional Dirichlet priors have been used for model selection in various applications. We introduce an innovative modeling approach utilizing product Dirichlet priors within the context of chain event graph models. This new method incorporates a separate Dirichlet process on a distinct space to establish explicit model space priors. We demonstrate that model selection can be performed efficiently using finite combinatorial methods, and establish theoretical similarities with the original P\'{e}cari index. We also address challenges posed by product Dirichlet processes through numerical integration and prove they have equivalent properties to process mixtures with Gaussian prior distributions. Finally, we compare our method to traditional methods with real data and examine the method's performance in settings of uncertainty.

Building on the, heavy ball method, this work delivers a comprehensive analysis of the half-step heavy ball method for strongly convex functions, offering a range of modifications that ensure convergence at an accelerated rate under specific conditions on the damping coefficient. The method's performance relies on a weighted average of full-step and half-step Newthon Raphson iterations, where the optimal damping coefficient allows for a smooth convergence rate transition between O(1/k) and O(1/k^2). The method's efficacy is further demonstrated through lower bounds on performance, showcasing that an optimal selection of damping coefficient is essential for achieving the desired convergence rate. The method is also extended to accommodate various types of non-linearity in the half-step damping mechanism, while maintaining its accelerated convergence properties. The method's performance is validated through a range of numerical examples, including convex and non-convex optimization problems.

This report explores the effectiveness of a distance sensor in wall-following applications. A physical robot was designed to execute a pre-programmed algorithm, aiming to maintain a consistent distance from a designated wall. The robot's behavior was observed on various tracks with different features, employing the same physical hardware but different views of the wall for the algorithm's input. By modifying the sensor's field of view, it was found that the same robot exhibited distinct behaviors when equipped with different sensors, demonstrating independence from the algorithm programmed to facilitate wall-following behavior.

Research on heavy-fermion alloys like CeAl$_2$ suggests using complex reflectance and impedance spectroscopy to study quasiparticle transport in various superconducting states beyond the simplest barter exchange. By applying these methods to CeAl$_2$, we've found an unusual difference between undoped and doped samples in their microwave frequency responses, which points to a more intricate interpretation of observed effects than previously considered necessary. In undoped samples, traditional understanding based on energy gap models successfully explains observed conductivities, whereas doped samples show parallel conductances alongside closed microwave circuitry at higher doping levels, which cannot be explained solely through established knowledge of superconducting gaps and radiative interactions. An alternative theoretical approach based on superconducting gap models involving paired and triplet components seems more likely to explain these findings, implying a more complex superconducting order in heavily doped samples.

This paper focuses on the well-suited nature of curvature flows under a group of transformations in nearly spherical surfaces. Once again, using the methods of Dirichlet and Neumann problems, it's demonstrated that this flow has a unique solution within a specific, adapted space. Although closely related to the findings of [HuiS] and [Pesenbacher], the underlying mathematical principles are considerably more intricate.

The underlying mechanisms of living systems, their growth, and evolution, can be deciphered by developing novel experimental protocols driven by data-driven and automated approaches.  We introduce a state-of-the-art experimental framework utilizing a cutting-edge technology to design and analyze the shape of living cellular aggregates and their response to external stimuli.  A reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to optimize experimental settings and ensure successful results, while a physics-informed neural network optimizes the physical models underlying these experiments.  Through autonomous exploration, our method consistently produces accurate and robust predictions, providing a promising solution for complex optimization problems in biological systems and potentially expanding the boundaries of physical law discovery.
All the necessary code to reproduce our results is available at https://github.com/jjansch/RLNN_on_living_aggregates

Researchers studied the conformally invariant models, including weighted quadrangulations, labeled trees, the uniform invariant Weingarten diagrams, the $O(N)$ sigma model's height formulation and self-avoiding polygons. They found that in the scaling limit these models all map to the same object, which can be viewed as equivalent to Liouville quantum gravity with proper normalization of parameters, and also to the so-called Vu polyhedron. This object is not well understood in mathematical terms, but researchers were able to derive important facts about it. These facts include that the number of certain types of discrete conformal structures on a given surface is constant, and that the distance between LQG distances and discrete conformal structure distances remains unclear. This work lays the foundation for exploring the properties of Vu polyhedrons, which contain significant conformal structure components. To explore this further, researchers used techniques, such as discrete conformal structure Laplacian, to study the behavior of specific components, like random surfaces, in the limit. These techniques were used across various models studied.

Recent advancements in high-throughout quantitative image analysis, known as radiomics, have been hindered by difficulties in image processing and data mining due to the complex nature of disease-related cellular environments. This complexity results in low image quality, numerous artifacts, and varying intensity scales. To overcome these issues, which have long hindered radiomics progress, a novel approach called DeepSynergy is presented. DeepSynergy leverages deep learning techniques to address several key challenges: (1) image enhancement through multi-scale and temporal analysis; (2) data standardization and segmentation via learned region-specific parameters, and (3) mining robust clinical data from varied datasets using multi-task, semi-supervised learning. DeepSynergy successfully demonstrated its advantages by achieving state-of-the-art performance in three applications: automated segmentation of region-specific lesions, identification of radiogenic features, and prediction of pathomic features using limited labeled data. This groundbreaking DeepSynergy approach marks a significant milestone in the radiomics community, offering a versatile and efficient image analysis and data mining framework that can be easily adapted to tackle various challenges related to image data diversity.

The observed photoproduction of kaons from hydrogen, $\gamma p \to K\Sigma$, was measured over a wide range of kinematics with regards to the angle between the photon beam and the kaon orbit.  These data, combined with an analysis of the properties of resonance particles using a specific matrix model, suggested the presence of several resonances within the observed data.  Specifically, the researchers identified the $\Sigma(1385)^0$-resonance as contributing to an observed peak at 1200 MeV, while a second peak at 1620 MeV was associated with either the $\Sigma(1550)^0$ or $\Sigma(1670)^0$ resonances.  A comparison of the data with an available theoretical model suggested that the latter resonance was more likely to explain the observed data.  Additionally, the researchers observed a broad, undetermined structure within the data, around 1750 MeV, which they speculated could be associated with the $\Sigma(1750)^0$ or $\Sigma(1775)^0$ resonances, or an as-yet-unknown resonant state.

This work establishes a reference point for a collaborative, iterative pre-processing pipeline development process. It outlines the specific sub-pipeline components, evaluates their effectiveness using a variety of metrics, and considers the impact of combining multiple pipelines on the classification performance. Furthermore, the project facilitates open participation, encouraging contributors to assess the current pipeline, propose improvements, and test new sub-pipelines or complete pipelines based on their own designs. By fostering a shared environment, the project aims to enhance the pre-processing pipeline through the collective efforts of the community.

Inflationary models that combine dark energy and dark matter into a single concept have drawn significant interest recently. Specifically, a model known as Chaplyhy Li-Munshi-Sokolov (CLMS) inflation has garnered attention for its potential to unify these phenomena. In this research, a thorough examination of noise-free spectral parameters for the CLMS model is presented, which originates from an interplay of a Gravitational wave and a Gravitational particle at the Planck scale. Analysis of noise-less data reveals distinctive features at low and intermediate w-values characterized by a complex power-law relationship. This unique characteristic enables a precise detection of the model's spectral parameters during future surveys such as LiteBIRD. In addition, a unified explanation for dark energy and dark matter within the framework of the CLMS model is presented. Specifically, a model-dependent expression for the dark energy and dark matter density ratios are derived and the potential for a proper quantum field theory description of dark matter is explored.

We introduce a generative model based on Gaussian variables to analyze patterns
in course enrollment, and develop an unsupervised approach for extracting groups
of students with similar enrollment histories from large educational datasets.
This method allows us to generate enrollment profiles for any new student using
only their individual enrollment history, without requiring labels or comparisons
to peers. Additionally, we can produce representations for each student and each
enrollment category, enabling comparison and grouping tasks. Experiments using
edX enrollment data reveal that our method segments students into distinct groups
based on their enrollment patterns, and that the probability-based student
classification process accurately identifies students with similar patterns.

A mathematical approach inspired by Pontryagin's principle is developed to identify stable Nash equilibria in vehicle platooning systems. This method combines optimization techniques with a constant Lyapunov function, utilizing the algebraic and differential structures inherent in the system's equations. In conjunction with a graph-theoretic analysis, it leads to the creation of a algorithm that systematically discovers all feasible Nash equilibria. Furthermore, the approach enables the determination of thresholds for the feasibility of summable constant vectors, thereby contributing to the understanding of the solvability of related optimality equations. Through a case study involving a system of nonlinear equations, the proposed approach demonstrates its potential to uncover insights regarding nonlinear problems. Finally, numerical results confirm the efficacy of the method in identifying stable states for a two-truck system and a tri-linear system.

This study presents a stochastic gradient descent algorithm with confidence acceleration for logistic regression, examining its performance and efficiency. The results show that this method achieves faster convergence rates and improved reliability compared to its counterparts. The rigorous analysis of this algorithm is a significant contribution to the field of probabilistic machine learning. To facilitate its use, the algorithm is implemented in a Python package, along with a accompanying benchmark test comparing its performance to established methods. The code and algorithm are provided as a supplementary resource for researchers and developers.

This study compares the ability of various language models to distinguish between human and computer-generated news headlines. It utilizes a unique dataset of 246,525 original headlines generated by the GPT-2 model and pairs them with their human counterparts. The analysis involves evaluating the performance of different models, including GPT-2 and its upgrades, as well as additional systems including Big Transfer Machine King, BERT, XLNet, and a range of neural networks. The results show that the largest GPT-3 models achieve 92% accuracy, and that GPT-2 and other advanced models can reach a accuracy of 90% or higher. The research also finds that certain metrics and data splitting methods can negatively impact the performance of models. The findings suggest that GPT-3 models can consistently outperform human-generated news headlines, and that the GPT-2 dataset and evaluation framework can serve as a valuable tool for evaluating the capabilities of language production systems. Additionally, the study's analysis of features and data splitting reveals new insights into how language production systems operate.

A multi-decade long theoretical debate has been ongoing about the nature of chiral key features present in certain materials known as Kagome materials. A new method of studying chiral properties in a specific type of Kagome material has shown that the properties can be associated with the presence of small magnetic moments that behave in a particular way. By examining how these moments are arranged on a two-dimensional surface, researchers have found that the properties can be described as gaps or sets of gaps in a magnetic spectrum, associated with the arrangement of triangles on that surface. When a particular type of Kagome structure is curved into a sphere, some theoretical predictions about the spectrum become ill-defined, but the method of study reveals that the gap related to the curvature increases with the density of the sphere's edges, suggesting that the chiral key features are related to the arrangement of triangles on a curved surface. A particular type of Kagome material has been found to have a particular type of magnetic arrangement, but the experiment does not provide direct information about the gap in a magnetic spectrum, rather it provides information about the density of the material's basic units, suggesting that the density of the material's basic units may be related to the gap in a magnetic spectrum. A new method of study has shown that the density of the material's basic units can provide information about the gap in a magnetic spectrum. Calibrating full-skymap antenna gains in large arrays with high redundancy is now possible with real-time schemes, leading some to believe that the per-gain antenna vector deconvolution inversion can be performed efficiently in real-time.  However, the aforementioned inversion has far-reaching implications, including introducing variance to individual antenna gains.  We investigated how the aforementioned real-time calibration schemes along with per-gain inversion techniques impact the variance of antenna gains in redundant arrays of various sizes and found that when using per-gain inversion based vector deconvolution methods the variance of gains doesn't remain uniform and is instead dependent on the geometry of the array and number of antennas.  Notably, our analysis of 1000-3000 antenna arrays indicated that the variance of gains is significantly higher than previously assumed and is on the same order of magnitude as the squint terms in the gain model, leading us to recommend additional measures to reduce variability and minimize its impact on time-variable gain models.

This study reimagines the traditional Markowitz framework for portfolio allocation using an autoencoding CGAN (ACGAN). The ACGAN model leverages machine learning to optimize portfolio optimization, unlike the Markowitz method which relies solely on mathematical formulas. By incorporating human investment preferences into the machine learning model, the ACGAN enhances portfolio allocation, compared to the standard Markowitz method. Furthermore, the ACGAN's learning process involves a vast search space, allowing it to robustly optimize portfolio diversification, particularly during turbulent market conditions. In a numerical experiment using S&P 500 stocks, the ACGAN model overperformed the Markowitz method in terms of overall return, delivering a 9.2% higher return with 1% higher risk.

The evolution of transition functions between different PDFs and their associated parton functions is essential in Fock-state calculations for both universal Wilson line moments and nonperturbative evolution equations.  In the VFN scheme, the evolution of the PDFs' universal Wilson line moments, represented by the functions $A_{ns}^{(r)}(N)$ for the color octet states, is well-documented.  However, the development of the transition functions $A_{gq}^{(r)}(N)$ between the PDFs and their associated parton functions, particularly for the color non-singlet states, has yet to be thoroughly researched.  In this work, the transition functions $A_{gq}^{(r)}(N)$ are studied in detail between the PDFs and their associated parton functions, specifically in the color non-singlet states.  Our findings show that the evolution of the transition functions $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$ is dominated by the Higgs-strahlung process.  By using the VPI parton distribution functions, our results indicate that the transition functions $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$ are positively correlated during the DGLAP evolution process.  Our research also reveals that the transition functions $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$ are negatively correlated during the time-reversal evolution process. Neural networks within a Bayesian framework offer an attractive option for classification tasks, especially when working with limited or imbalanced data. The primary benefit of the Bayesian framework lies in its posterior uncertainty distribution, which yields compelling accuracy yet generates inconveniencing computational overhead and a complex, unwieldy posterior distribution that has gone largely unexplored. In an effort to harness the advantages of the Bayesian framework without the drawbacks, this research proposes a novel approximation technique called FPC-MAP. The proposed method approximates the complex posterior distribution by leveraging variational approximations and Expectation-Maximization algorithms. FPC-MAP generates predictions based on the MAP approximation of the posterior mean and induces sparsity through a spike-and-slice variational approximation of the posterior covariance matrix. The posterior uncertainty is quantified using ELBO optimization, while the approximation of the posterior covariance matrix is based on the proportion of'slice' probability mass. FPC-MAP achieves a balance between accuracy and computational efficiency by leveraging a variational'split' approximation, with the posterior concentration parameter determining the nature of the approximation. FPC-MAP is benchmarked against leading competitors, including Monte-Carlo sampling and variational approximations, in an extensive battery of tests. The results show FPC-MAP consistently achieves competitive accuracy on synthetic and real-world datasets while maintaining efficient computational speed.

Despite the extensive presence of user-generated content (UGC) on social media, accessing certain platforms or content is restricted by barriers such as geographical or linguistic obstacles. Breakable barriers in social media, like required interactions or underlying systems, can be identified and circumvented using search engines to reach the desired UGC. We introduce UGC4NLP, a dataset comprising 472k English questions gathered from Reddit to investigate web-based UGC acquisition on social media. These questions, designed to solve barriers on StackExchange and Reddit platforms, are analyzed in relation to their actual solutions, allowing for the evaluation of acquisition methods and detection of patterns that can aid in overcoming barriers.

A new hypergraph tensor computation framework is developed to efficiently
calculate spectral characteristics like the eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
The tensor join technique expands on the potential computational capabilities
of tensors by incorporating vertices with multiple corresponding labels, thus
enhancing tensor applications to multi-label data sets. The proposed method
utilizes the tensor join along with the alternating least squares method to improve
spectral property calculations, allowing for the incorporation of additional
features like vertex modification without affecting the network's structure.
The tensor join's applications to multi-label data sets reveal improved performance
in comparison to standard tensors, while the incorporation of the alternating
least squares method aids in eigenproblem solving not readily amenable to existing
algorithms.

INSIST, installed at the Special Astronomical Observatory, is a 1.65m telescope equipped with a special instrumentation called SD Cam, which consists of six cameras functioning as a hyper-spectral imager. This instrument covers the wavelength range from 0.4 to 2.3 $\mu$m and offers an unprecedented combination of spatial, spectral, and temporal qualities. With its unique layout, SD Cam enables simultaneous data collection in six channels, allowing for quality comparisons and merging capabilities similar to those of the Hubble Space Telescope. However, INSIST's superior quality is expected when comparing single-channel performance, as the merged data from all channels will surpass even the advanced imaging capabilities of the Hubble Space Telescope across various wavelengths. Here we introduce INSIST, its current status, and highlight a sample hyper-spectral image taken of the Crab Nebula, which is also compared to a publicly available Hubble image. Additionally, we outline INSIST's initial scientific objectives and introduce a public database containing hyper-spectral imaging (HSI) data. Finally, a public code for merging and de-interlacing INSIST's data is provided, enabling researchers to maximize the instrument's imaging capabilities.

In clinical trials, smooth changes over time in continuous measures are often observed, which can be effectively represented by constrained longitudinal data analysis using natural cubic splines within a linear mixed model framework. This approach can be incorporated into the mixed model via a random effect Q matrix, which can be estimated by various optimization methods. Originally, constrained least squares was developed to minimize time-varying covariate effects, which can also be achieved by adjusting the model setup. By transforming the problem into a constrained least squares form, two optimizers - the conjugate gradient and the interior point methods - can be used to find the optimal solution. These methods have been found to perform better than traditional quadratic optimization methods. Furthermore, two algorithms are proposed to adapt the interior point method for handling different types of constraints and are found to be efficient and accurate. After obtaining the optimal constrained estimates, diagnostic checks can be conducted on the model using standard tools, which can also be used for making predictions or forecasts. Examples and illustrations of these methods are also provided.

A novel method called conformational space annealing is introduced to enhance the exploration of reaction pathways through molecular simulation. The approach utilizes an arbitrary reference reaction pathway, anchoring the simulation to known intermediates, and performs an extensive spatial analysis to identify a more efficient and direct route between initial and final states. The method is successfully applied to three challenging systems: the isomerization of pentacene upon irradiation, the rotation of hexagonal boron nitride monolayers, and the transformation of chlorophenol from trans to cis. Our research details the methods' implementation and highlights the advantages of each case study. The conformational space annealing technique displays improved efficiency in sampling reaction pathways, reducing computational burdens, and offering high flexibility in accommodating diverse systems.

In this research, we show that the $L^{n/(n-1)}$ bounds derived from parabolic Hessian equations have been naturally extended to the fully nonlinear parabolic equations sectorially convex towards second-order elliptic operators, as well as towards a range of second-order elliptic operators with positive limited convexity. Additionally, the $L^{n/(n-1)}$ bounds are extended to the fully nonlinear elliptic equations in the context of H\"older continuous solutions.

In a recent study, we demonstrated that a specific subset of terms generated by simply typed lambda-calculus can be achieved using a particular encoding, which maps type constructors and elements to lambda-terms, also showing that this subset has limited expressiveness when used with untyped reductions. The current paper extends these findings by examining a modified encoding for a typed lambda-calculus with weak equality and weak inductive types in a coinductive framework, also offering an alternative, elementary proof of its weak expressiveness. Unlike previous research, which focused on substantial reductions, this study delves into finer details, specifically the implications of omitting certain components, like weak inductive types or equality, and provides coinductive, automatic procedures for determining expressiveness. The findings presented offer a novel method for assessing the weak expressiveness of a specific, syntactically defined encoding, also highlighting the significance of using a coinductive approach for these kinds of problems.

We apply the concept of Lions-type measure derivatives to a family of nonlinear parabolic equations, demonstrating their relationship to a family of stochastic differential equations. This connection leads to a measure-valued process that serves as a factor for the equation's solution, involving an integral of a given function times the measure. By leveraging the Karatzas-Shreve formula, we establish a factor process, and our approach results in a simplified proof of a prior result from ME-CritRev and introduces a novel outcome that the factor process is a martingale when the diffusion term is Brownian motion. Lastly, we identify the measure derivative of a stochastic differential equation and explore its utility in generating a Girsanov density.

The discussion revolves around various topological spaces derived from ideal lattices, specifically those associated with group theories. These spaces include the lattice itself, its completion, a specific type of hull-kernel topology associated with normal subgroups, and other topological spaces related to quasicoincidence closed subgroups. It is demonstrated that various spaces obtained in this manner fall into distinct categories such as $T_0$, $T_1$, $T_2$, or $T_3$. particular emphasis is placed on analyzing the relationship between normal subgroups and compactness, thus providing general frameworks for applying previous results to specific applications, including the examination of $T_3$-plots in hereditary torsion groups and specific subgroup topologies in group theory. The analysis also raises questions about the nature of quasicoincidence closed subgraphs in various contexts.

The increasing adoption of databaseless in-memory grammar-based compilers has led to a growing need for a robust, interactive generation system that produces valid output based on user-inputted database entries. Current systems fall short in execution accuracy when faced with missing database components, resulting in incorrect application of production rules. In this research, we present an approach that efficiently reconstructs the missing database components during execution, allowing for accurate rule application and performance optimization. Our proposed framework significantly improves execution speed, boasting execution times 3.7 to 7 times faster than state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to correctly process input sequences in the presence of missing database components, resulting in up to 100% successful parsing rate as opposed to 75% with existing techniques.

This research introduces a collision avoidance strategy for autonomous robots that works effectively even when their movements are hard to predict. By incorporating actual error measurements from each robot into the calculation of potential collisions, this method can accurately assess and respond to sudden changes in motion. The technique ensures consistent results by converting the error data into a unified format, making it a reliable and efficient solution for avoiding collisions in complex and unpredictable environments. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through collision avoidance simulations involving multiple robots moving unpredictably.

Andromeda XXV, a recently discovered dwarf spheroidal galaxy with extremely low light emission, is one of the brightest dwarf satellites of the Andromeda galaxy. Studies of stellar populations in this galaxy have determined the presence of an old metal-poor population. Our research aims to understand the structural properties of Andromeda XXV by analyzing its brightness and surface brightness profiles using data from the Pan-Andromeda Archaeological Survey for the galaxy's outer regions. The results of our analysis indicate Andromeda XXV has a unique mass-to-light ratio compared to other dwarf spheroidals, featuring an \(r_{\rm half}\) radius of approximately 34 pec and a surface brightness of around 19.06 mag arcsec$^{-1}$ in the $I$ band. The Andromeda XXV galaxy has an Sersic index of about 1 and a brightness profile that differs from that of other galaxies. The findings also suggest the presence of an extended stellar halo in Andromeda XXV. Our research further indicates that Andromeda XXV has a density that falls within the third quartile when compared to other dwarf spheroidals. The results of our research imply the presence of an elongated and possibly irregular shape in the galaxy with distinct features in its central and outer areas. The unique mass properties and brightness profile of Andromeda XXV support theories that it once hosted a significant amount of dark matter and experienced either a gas enrichment event or

In recent research, non-orthogonal sequences have emerged as a promising solution to tackle the issue of grant-free access in uplink transmission, leveraging their unique properties to enhance sequence multiplexing. To build upon this finding, this study delves into the potential of non-orthogonal sequences for grant-free access in uplink transmission. Initially, the method for generating orthogonal sequences is adapted to produce non-orthogonal sequences, and their auto-correlation and cross-correlation characteristics are analyzed and mathematically derived. Notably, non-orthogonal sequences are found to offer performance benefits and increased sequence multiplexing efficiency. To further optimize performance, sequence design is formulated as an optimization problem, taking into account both auto-correlation and cross-correlation phase shifts. By integrating the method for generating orthogonal sequences, the optimal phase shifts are determined, and their effectiveness is verified through simulation results showing improved sequence design outcomes.

Highly simplified equations for adiabatic moist air dynamics are derived using the consistent constant $\kappa$ approximation of the saturation vapor pressure formula. This theoretical framework assumes that thermodynamic potentials remain a perfect invariant throughout non-electrolyte adiabatic systems. Utilizing this theory, the simplified phase transitions in the presence of latent heat are modeled, and predictions are compared to actual values from relevant research. A perfect constant $\kappa$ approximation of the saturation pressure is used, and results demonstrate that this theoretical model effectively replicates more complex simulation results while maintaining a high level of accuracy, specifically in simulating phase transitions and temperatures. Furthermore, the theoretical model predicts that system states will always remain in thermodynamic equilibrium and, consequently, never experience non-thermalized vapor state fluctuations. As such, the role of temperature fluctuations in the emergence of two-mode condensate temperature spectra remains unclear and requires further investigation.

The exterior algebra of an $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-algebra is an essential component in the matroid-multiplicity link, a concept developed within the framework of noncommutative algebra over $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$. This idea involves extending both classical notions and notations based on the exterior algebra of a linear matroid to the more generalized $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-linear setting. The $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-algebra's exterior algebra is analogous to the exterior algebra of an $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-matroid, which shares similarities with the free exterior algebra of a linear matroid, excluding scalar multiplication. The exterior algebra of an $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-algebra can be seen as the limit of the exterior algebras of $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-linear matroids as the rank approaches a singular value. The scalar multiplication in this context can be seen as the limit of the exterior multiplicities of these matroids as the rank approaches a singular value. Furthermore, the free $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-algebra of a matroid generalizes the free exterior algebra of an $\mathbb{F}_1^{\pm}$-linear matroid, excluding scalar multiplication.
